records.title: Colorado Privacy Act (C.R.S. §§ 6-1-1301 et seq.)
records.applicability_summary: The CPA may apply to controllers and processors conducting business in Colorado or targeting Colorado residents when statutory processing thresholds and other conditions are met. The Attorney General describes thresholds based on processing personal data of at least 100,000 Colorado consumers, or at least 25,000 consumers where revenue or discounts are derived from sale of personal data. Entity-specific exemptions and data exclusions require legal review.
triggers: Colorado business activity or products/services targeted to Colorado residents
Personal data processing meeting statutory consumer thresholds
Processing sensitive data, targeted advertising, sale or profiling activities
obligations: Transparent privacy notices and purpose disclosures
Data minimization and reasonable security practices
Consumer access, correction, deletion and portability rights
Universal opt-out handling where required
Data protection assessments for specified high-risk processing
Affirmative consent before processing sensitive data where required
uncertainties: Confirm current threshold calculations, statutory exemptions and controller/processor roles with counsel
Confirm final status of amendments to 4 CCR 904-3 and all amendments to Part 13
Determine whether any processing is employment, commercial-context or otherwise excluded

records.title: SB26-189 Automated Decision-Making Technology

sources.authority: Colorado Attorney General / Department of Law

records.applicability_summary: Enacted legislation that repeals and reenacts Colorado's prior AI consequential-decision provisions with requirements for developers and deployers of automated decision-making technology that materially influences consequential decisions. Applicability depends on covered technology, consequential decision domains, entity role and statutory definitions. The stated effective date is January 1, 2027.
triggers: Developing or deploying ADMT that materially influences consequential decisions
Covered decisions involving education, employment, housing, financial/lending services, insurance, health care or essential government services/public benefits
Providing or receiving covered ADMT technical documentation
obligations: Developer technical documentation on intended uses, training-data categories, known limitations and appropriate use/human review
Notice of material ADMT updates or modifications to deployers
At least three-year retention of records necessary to demonstrate compliance
Deployer consumer notices and post-adverse-outcome explanations within statutory timeframes
Consumer requests for relevant personal data, correction and meaningful human review/reconsideration
uncertainties: Confirm final rule adoption and exact operative text before the January 1, 2027 effective date
A federal court order in xAI v. Weiser contains a temporary enforcement stay referring to SB24-205 and replacement/amending legislation; counsel must assess its scope and current status
Confirm statutory definitions, exclusions, thresholds and developer/deployer allocation for the actual use case

records.title: HB26-1263 Conversational AI Service Operator Requirements (Chatbot Safety Act)

sources.authority: Colorado Attorney General / Department of Law

records.applicability_summary: Enacted requirements for operators of conversational AI services accessible to the general public that primarily simulate human conversation and interaction. The Colorado Attorney General describes the law as taking effect January 1, 2027. Applicability depends on the service, operator role, user population and statutory definitions.
triggers: Making a conversational AI service publicly available or offering it to consumers
Users or account holders may be minors
Service includes adaptive textual, visual or aural conversation
obligations: Disclose to users that they are interacting with AI
Use commercially reasonable or generally accepted methods to estimate user age as required
Implement specified safeguards and account/privacy tools for minors
Implement protocols for prompts involving suicidal ideation or self-harm
Submit annual reports to the Attorney General as required
Do not represent outputs as equivalent to services of licensed or certified professionals
uncertainties: Confirm exact effective-date provisions and any referendum or litigation developments
Confirm final rulemaking and annual-report details
Determine whether the service meets the statutory definition and whether exemptions apply

records.title: Proposed 2026 ADMT and Chatbot Safety Rules
records.applicability_summary: The Colorado Department of Law reports that proposed draft rules implementing SB26-189 and HB26-1263 were filed on August 11, 2026; an interim draft was released October 6; a regulatory analysis was released October 21; and a formal rulemaking hearing was held October 26, 2026. As of the November 2, 2026 source review, the agency page states that it is drafting the final rules after considering comments. This record tracks rulemaking only and does not represent final adopted rules.
triggers: Colorado ADMT or conversational AI service operation
Final rulemaking, hearing notices, adopted rules or agency guidance are published
obligations: Monitor formal rulemaking, hearing outcomes and adopted rule text
Reconcile final rules against the statutory control catalogue
uncertainties: Final rules had not been posted on the agency rulemaking page as of the November 2, 2026 review; recheck the agency and Secretary of State records
Do not treat draft language as binding law

records.jurisdiction: United States District Court, District of Colorado
records.title: xAI LLC v. Weiser, No. 1:26-cv-01515 — temporary enforcement stay monitor

sources.authority: Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse / RECAP docket materials
U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado docket mirror

records.applicability_summary: An April 27, 2026 minute order temporarily restrained the Colorado Attorney General from initiating enforcement, including investigations, for alleged violations of SB24-205 or legislation replacing or amending it enacted during the 2026 legislative session, for the period specified in the order relative to a future ruling on a preliminary-injunction motion. This record is a litigation monitor, not a conclusion that any entity or law is exempt or unenforceable.
triggers: New docket entries, preliminary-injunction motion or ruling
Final ADMT/chatbot rulemaking or later legislation
Any planned reliance on the stay for a compliance decision
obligations: Recheck the official PACER docket and obtain counsel's interpretation before relying on the order
Track the order's exact temporal and statutory scope and any subsequent modification or termination
uncertainties: The order's scope regarding SB26-189 and HB26-1263 requires legal interpretation
Available docket mirror last showed a later procedural entry dated October 2, 2026; PACER must be checked for subsequent activity
Do not infer that the stay suspends statutory effective dates or private obligations

records.jurisdiction: United States, voluntary standards and guidance
records.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0

sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology

records.applicability_summary: NIST AI RMF 1.0 is voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific guidance intended to help organizations manage AI risks. It is not itself a generally binding law. It may become relevant through contracts, procurement terms, policies or incorporation into applicable requirements.
triggers: Contract, procurement or policy requires alignment
A law or regulator references a framework or equivalent standard
obligations: Use Govern, Map, Measure and Manage concepts where adopted
Track NIST's stated revision work and future framework updates
uncertainties: Confirm whether a contract, procurement term or applicable law makes any specific framework requirement binding
